item.text:
**8B.4 Research Note: Félix Tshisekedi in 2024**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning weakly positive on civilian technocratic staffing, but weak on security-command execution. The clearest positive evidence is that Tshisekedi did place some competent people in key civilian roles and backed a few technical oversight/reform mechanisms. The clearest negative evidence is that the military/security ecosystem remained fragmented, proxy-dependent, and only received late corrective reshuffling.

| Polarity | Claim-level item | Publisher / date | Recoverable URL | Short summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Judith Suminwa named prime minister as a technocratic, competent choice | Reuters, 2024-04-01 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/ | Reuters reported Tshisekedi appointed Planning Minister Judith Suminwa as PM. That is concrete evidence that he elevated a policy-facing technocrat rather than only a loyalist. | 8B.4 |
| Positive | Presidency said Suminwa was chosen for skills and development-planning experience | Ministère de la Communication et Médias, 2024-04-01 | https://communication.gouv.cd/actualites/communications-du-gouvernement/18/madame-judith-suminwa-tuluka-nommee-premiere-ministre-de-la-republique-democratique-du-congo | The presidency framed the appointment explicitly as competence-based and inclusionary. This is self-reporting, so it counts as weaker than Reuters, but it still supports the technocratic staffing reading. | 8B.4 |
| Positive | Finance ministry staffed by a career public-finance technocrat | ACP / Administration des Finances, 2024-05-30 | https://adminfinances.cd/ProfilMin.php | The finance ministry profile describes Doudou Fwamba as a career official with economics/public-finance training and over a decade in the ministry. That supports a merit-based appointment in a strategic portfolio. | 8B.4 |
| Positive | Education reform design emphasized merit-based recruitment and stronger information systems | World Bank, 2024-02-28 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes | The World Bank project for primary education included merit-based teacher recruitment, qualified female teachers, better information systems, and decentralized planning. This is good evidence of executive willingness to use competence-oriented implementation machinery. | 8B.4 |
| Positive | Tshisekedi backed Court of Accounts oversight and anti-corruption control | Présidence RDC, 2024-10-07 | https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes | The Court of Accounts’ leadership publicly credited Tshisekedi with supporting the control function and anti-corruption oversight. This is executive-hosted and therefore not independent proof, but it still supports a willingness to empower oversight institutions. | 8B.4 |
| Positive | IMF program translated into concrete fiscal and administrative mechanisms | IMF, 2024-07-15 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/15/democratic-republic-of-the-congo-2024-article-iv-consultation-sixth-review-under-the-551892 | IMF said the government was cleaning the civil-service register with biometrics, improving treasury/expenditure-chain controls, and making slow but real progress on reforms. This is evidence that Tshisekedi’s administration had some capable policy execution capacity. | 8B.4 |
| Negative | Cabinet formation was delayed by internal jostling for jobs | Reuters, 2024-05-29 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/DR-Congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/ | Reuters said months of internal bargaining delayed the cabinet. That points to coalition/patronage pressures still shaping appointments, which weakens a clean competence-first reading. | 8B.4 |
| Negative | Security apparatus remained disordered and proxy-heavy | Reuters, 2024-07-17 | https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/ | Reuters reported officers describing weak logistics, demoralized troops, and reliance on poorly trained, undisciplined Wazalendo militias that the army did not control. This is strong counterevidence that Tshisekedi had not effectively empowered a disciplined execution team in the security sphere. | 8B.4 |
| Mixed | Late-year reshuffle suggests corrective action, but also confirms earlier command weakness | Reuters, 2024-12-20 | https://theprint.in/world/congolese-president-sacks-military-top-brass-in-major-reshuffle/2411531/ | Tshisekedi replaced the army chief, military intelligence head, and many senior officers. This can be read as remedial professionalization, but it also shows the prior command structure was not working well. | 8B.4 |

**Synthesis**

- Best positive reading: Tshisekedi did place some technically competent people in top civilian roles and backed reform/oversight mechanisms that look execution-oriented rather than purely patronage-driven.
- Best negative reading: the security side of the state still looked fragmented, proxy-dependent, and weakly controlled for much of 2024, with only a late corrective reshuffle.
- Net: evidence is mixed, with a modest case for competence in civilian economic administration and a stronger case against effective, disciplined execution in security governance.

**Search gap**

- I did not find a direct, independent source that reveals Tshisekedi’s internal selection criteria beyond these appointments and reform readouts.
- The strongest positive items are partly self-reported or programmatic; the strongest negative items come from Reuters and human-rights/reporting sources and are more concrete on actual execution problems.
